problem.name: QUIESCENCE_COUNTER_SURFACE_COVERAGE_GAP
observed: The pre-hardening runtime quiescence probe compared only derived free swarm/LIVE_METRICS.json worker usage before/after the bounded window.
The nearly co-temporal LIVE_METRICS snapshot reports openrouter/free requests=288 while SYSTEM_ANALYSIS_LIVE shared_provider_budget reports openrouter total_requests=4230.
tools/free_swarm_quota.py increments provider_state.total_requests inside acquire() before a provider request proceeds.

The shared budget also contains non-provider/tool lanes such as github/arxiv/crossref, so an unfiltered all-row digest would be stronger than the canonical provider-stop claim and could reject unrelated permitted source-tool activity.
problem.inference: LIVE_METRICS worker usage and the shared provider-budget attempt counters are not identical evidence surfaces; derived worker-metric stability alone is insufficient for the declared zero provider-counter-delta closure condition. Direct shared-budget evidence must be scoped to the provider names governed by canonical FREE_PROVIDER_ADMISSION rather than every tool lane in the shared DB.
problem.hypothesis: Direct read-only sampling of provider_budget.sqlite3 cumulative counters plus unexpired leases, filtered to the canonical FREE_PROVIDER_ADMISSION provider set, closes the provider-attempt measurement gap while retaining LIVE_METRICS as an independent secondary surface and allowing unrelated source-tool counters to move.
problem.counterhypothesis: If every provider-capable request were fully represented in LIVE_METRICS with no lag or omitted lanes, direct shared-budget sampling would be redundant. The observed 288 vs 4230 OpenRouter request counts falsify identity/equivalence of the two surfaces at the current snapshot, though they do not by themselves prove which individual process caused each attempt.
